summary: Lassen Volcanic lookout: an earlier station burned in 1915; the 1924 cabin was staffed by John Gransbury; the register says it was demolished in 1956 with nothing left, while Forest Lookouts says a trail crew burned it; the summit is a 7.4-mile round-trip hike.

facts.agency: National Park Service, Lassen Volcanic National Park
facts.status_note: The register says the tower was demolished in 1956 and nothing remains at the site; Forest Lookouts says a trail maintenance crew burned it that year.

access.note: Hiking trail in Lassen Volcanic National Park, starting at the Brokeoff Mountain parking lot near the southwest entrance.

visit.trail_note: Round trip 7.4 miles, about 6 hours; rocky, forested and alpine terrain; considered one of the toughest trails in the park.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1915 station was under the Lassen National Forest, as the Forest Lookouts header shows; the register lists the National Park Service, which runs Lassen Volcanic National Park today.

The register says the tower was demolished in 1956 and nothing remains; Forest Lookouts says a trail maintenance crew burned it that year. Both accounts are reported; the sources do not settle which is right.

notes_for_editor: Elevations disagree and no source explains why: the register gives 9,127 ft (2,782 m) for the site, which is the record value; a 1933 newspaper gives 9,232 ft; a 1935 newspaper gives 9,400 ft; the NPS trail listing runs up to 9,235 ft. The record's material 'wood' is not stated for the 1924 cabin in any source read; the 1915 station was a frame platform under canvas. The FFLOS page's coordinates are garbled (S and W notation), so the record's coordinates were left unchanged. The 1934 and 1935 newspapers place Gransbury on the lookout from 1924 to at least 1935; the sources do not say when he left. A social-media post cites NPS archive photos of the 1956 demolition; not used because it was not verified. The 1956 end conflicts: the register says demolished, Forest Lookouts says burned by a trail maintenance crew; the story reports both.
